title: Add output, jobs and option errors to the argument parser
task: Extend parse_args(args) in src/lib.rs, keeping its signature and the existing verbose/output/inputs fields. Add a public field jobs: usize to Options; it is 1 when not given. Rules, applied left to right: -v and --verbose set verbose. -o FILE, --output FILE and --output=FILE set output; -j N, --jobs N and --jobs=N set jobs. In the separated forms the next argument is always the value, even if it starts with '-'. The last occurrence of a repeated option wins. N must be a decimal integer >= 1, otherwise return an error. An option that needs a value but is the last argument is an error; so is --output= or --jobs= with an empty value. A lone '-' is an input. '--' ends option parsing: every later argument is an input, even if it starts with '-'. Any other argument that starts with '-' is an unknown option and an error; this includes grouped short flags such as -vo and --verbose=yes. Other arguments are inputs, kept in order. Error messages must contain the offending text: the whole argument for an unknown option, the option name (such as -o or --jobs) for a missing or empty value, and the value for an invalid N. Add unit tests.
